transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-09
Time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Redwood SE), Morgan Reyes (Lumina Eng Mgr), Diego Alvarez (Lumina ML Eng), Priya Singh (Lumina Platform), Sam O'Neill (Lumina SRE)

Summary (auto):
Quick sync to review staging metrics from last integration run, verify SDK function-calling behavior with structured output, and surface KV-caching and batching tuning for the pilot. Agreed to run larger synthetic load tests and validate schema stability.

Topics: SDK integration, function/tool calling, structured-output schema stability, KV cache effects, latency vs cost trade-offs, next steps for pilot scale run.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Alex Chen: hey team, good to see everyone, thanks for coming on short notice, uh we got about 45 minutes, maybe 50, so we'll try to keep tight. quick roll call?
[00:08] Morgan Reyes: Morgan here, Diego, Priya S, Sam here for Lumina.
[00:12] Alex Chen: awesome, alex here, priya and jordan on the redwood side.
[00:16] Priya Patel: hi all. quick agenda: one, review the staging run results; two, function calling and structured output oddities diego saw; three, kv cache / batching tuning; four, next steps. sound good?
[00:27] Diego Alvarez: yeah i'm mostly curious about the structured outputs, we saw some missing fields and occasional extra arrays.
[00:32] Jordan Lee: okay good, we reproduced earlier problems on our side. just to set expectation, some of this comes from schema enforcement in the SDK versus the model output itself.
[00:40] Morgan Reyes: just a small ask up front, can we prioritize latency numbers for p95 and p99 with and without prefix cache? that's the metric execs want.
[00:49] Priya Patel: yep we'll surface p50/p95/p99. on the last run we had two configs: baseline (no kv) and prefix-kv enabled, both on shared staging dedicated pool. i'll paste the sheet after.
[00:58] Sam O'Neill: quick note, our staging traffic skew is heavier sequence length, so tail latency is worse than you might see in prod.
[01:06] Alex Chen: good call, please annotate that in the sheet. ok priya, can you walk results?
[01:12] Priya Patel: sure. baseline had median of 210ms per token generation for the invoked model variant, p95 around 1.8s and p99 at about 3.9s. with prefix-kv enabled for repeated contexts we saw median drop to 140ms, p95 1.1s p99 2.3s. those are rough numbers because the staging pool had some cross-tenant noise.
[01:34] Diego Alvarez: wait p99 2.3s with kv, that's still high for our interactive use case, the UI needs under 1.5s for 99th or users complain.
[01:42] Priya Patel: understood. two levers: further kv warmup (longer TTL + prefetch on session open) and aggressive batching/smaller sequence work to reduce overhead. also model variant choice matters — we used the quantized v2 variant; there is a faster low-latency flavor but it trades off some quality.
[02:01] Morgan Reyes: can you quantify the quality delta? we can't degrade NLU by 8-10% without product sign-off.
[02:06] Jordan Lee: right — for the low-latency variant we saw a minor drop in intent accuracy on your eval set, about 2.5% absolute on the current prompts. we can run a focused eval suite if you want an exact confusion matrix.
[02:17] Diego Alvarez: yes please, send the eval run results.
[02:20] Alex Chen: action: priya will run targeted eval on low-latency flavor and share numbers.
[02:24] Priya Patel: noted.
[02:26] 
[02:27] Morgan Reyes: switching to function calling — diego saw function mismatches, can you describe?
[02:31] Diego Alvarez: yeah, so with the SDK call pattern we call Redwood.invoke with tool definitions and we expect structured JSON back. roughly 10% of calls returned trailing commas or duplicated fields like "items": [..], "items": [..] which then breaks our parser. sometimes the SDK validated it but then the model output included extraneous tokens.
[02:49] Jordan Lee: mmhmm, this is a couple-layer problem. the SDK does a best-effort JSON extraction, but if the model emits commentary or extra tokens outside the function response the extractor can mis-attribute. also some of the model temperature/noise in staging made it more likely.
[03:02] Priya Patel: we also noticed the tool schema you provided has optional fields with loose types, that makes the parser more permissive. tightening the schema will reject malformed outputs earlier.
[03:11] Diego Alvarez: how do we tighten without breaking the conversations midstream?
[03:14] Jordan Lee: two strategies: stricter tool schemas + post-validate step in your runtime that rejects and asks for a re-call (we have an auto-retry pattern), or force function-calling-only mode where model is constrained to return only the function payload. the latter reduces flexibility but yields much cleaner JSON.
[03:29] Sam O'Neill: are there rate or cost implications with re-call retries? because our cost projection for pilot already close to budget.
[03:35] Priya Patel: retries add tokens and latency. our recommendation is to combine schema tightening with a single auto-retry and a caching of last-good output for brisk UX. that keeps retry cost low.
[03:45] Morgan Reyes: could you share the auto-retry implementation snippet?
[03:48] Priya Patel: yes i'll post the SDK snippet in the shared doc, it's basically an SDK option: "ensure_structured": true, "max_function_retries": 1, plus a transform that runs jsonschema validation.
[03:59] Diego Alvarez: the other thing we saw: streaming + function calling has an odd cut where partial tool payload appears in stream then final commit changes keys. so our client parser was confused.
[04:11] Jordan Lee: streaming and function-calls is tricky; streaming emits token-by-token, and our SDK buffers until the function close token. sometimes intermediate events show up, note this is expected but SDK exposes stable event to client once done. it sounds like your parser was handling partial events.
[04:24] Priya Singh: yeah we were acting on partial events to show progressive UI, maybe that's the source. we can tweak to only handle full "function_complete" event.
[04:32] Alex Chen: good catch. we'll mark that in the action items.
[04:35] 
[04:36] Morgan Reyes: Kevin — sorry who's leading the KV config on staging? (crosstalk)
[04:39] Sam O'Neill: i'll own that. i started with 30m TTL, maybe that's too short.
[04:44] Priya Patel: for session-heavy flows we recommend session-TTL 6 hours for warm prefixes, and an initial prefetch on session start of top-3 recent prompts. in staging we didn't prefetch, so first hits still paid full cost.
[04:56] Diego Alvarez: for prefetch how do we control cost? prefetch could increase token count.
[04:59] Jordan Lee: prefetch is targeted; it only pulls small prefixes (first 128 tokens) and it's amortized because subsequent messages reuse KV. think of it like priming the cache. also instrument to stop prefetch if user leaves early.
[05:11] Morgan Reyes: ok that sounds acceptable.
[05:13] Alex Chen: on batching: we saw in your logs you had very low batch sizes because the client wanted immediate responses. we can do micro batching local to the runtime with 20–30ms wait to increase throughput without visible UX hit.
[05:25] Sam O'Neill: but for interactive flows, adding 20–30ms might be noticeable. can we do adaptive batching — only batch when concurrency is high?
[05:31] Priya Patel: yes adaptive batching based on QPS thresholds is supported in the runtime. also recommend per-route policies; for interactive route set max_wait 15ms lower threshold, for background worker route set 50ms.
[05:42] Diego Alvarez: what's the tool chain to configure that? is it in the console or config file?
[05:46] Jordan Lee: both: you can set in the route config via API or Console -> Routing -> per-route inference config. we'll share a sample route json.
[05:53] Morgan Reyes: one more ask — privacy and KMS. our security folks insisted on seeing KMS/HSM integration for private deployment. even in staging we want logs scrubbed.
[06:04] Alex Chen: noted. Redwood private supports KMS integrations; for hosted we offer envelope encryption with customer-managed KMS. priya, can you link the security pack?
[06:11] Priya Patel: yes i'll share SOC2+KMS whitepaper. i'll add instructions for scrubbing pii from logs and redaction hooks.
[06:18] 
[06:19] Diego Alvarez: regarding structured output mismatches, can we run a quick live example now? i can paste one failing transcript.
[06:24] Morgan Reyes: sure go ahead diego.
[06:26] Diego Alvarez: pasted into chat - example request: ask model to return {"intent":..., "entities": [...]} we got back something like {"intent": "order_create", "entities": [{..}], , "items": []} with a stray comma then repeated items field.
[06:39] Jordan Lee: ok that is consistent with tokenization noise. quick mitigation: add an output sanitization step that strips duplicate keys and runs strict json repair. not ideal but reduces pipeline failures. second, lowering temperature to 0.0-0.2 for structured outputs helps a lot.
[06:51] Priya Singh: we run at 0.3 in staging because we wanted some paraphrase, but for function outputs we can set lower.
[06:58] Alex Chen: recommended default for function-calls in pilot: temp 0.0 - 0.15, ensure_structured true, max_function_retries 1.
[07:08] Morgan Reyes: ok noted.
[07:10] 
[07:11] Alex Chen: circling back to telemetry — we want to make sure you have trace ids from the SDK to map to your infra traces. did the last run include those?
[07:19] Sam O'Neill: partially, we got request ids but not per-token trace ids, so hard to map token-level spikes.
[07:25] Jordan Lee: SDK has a debug flag to emit token-level timestamps, but it can be verbose. we'll share sample logging config. for pilot i'd suggest request-level plus per-stage timing (invoke start/kvcache hit/batch wait/response end).
[07:40] Diego Alvarez: that should be enough.
[07:42] 
[07:43] Priya Patel: final notes — we'll: 1) share benchmark sheet (p50/p95/p99 with/without kv), 2) post SDK snippet for ensure_structured + retry, 3) route config examples for adaptive batching, 4) security doc and KMS instructions.
[07:58] Morgan Reyes: timeline?
[07:59] Priya Patel: i'll upload items 1-3 by 2026-11-12 and security doc by 2026-11-13.
[08:06] Alex Chen: and Lumina will run the synthetic 1k qps test and report by 2026-11-13.
[08:11] Diego Alvarez: yeah we'll schedule that overnight run.
[08:14] Morgan Reyes: ok any blockers for rolling to a bigger pilot? our execs want to see stable p99 under 1.5s for interactive route.
[08:24] Jordan Lee: we think it's doable with prefetch + lower temp + adaptive batching + low-latency model variant if quality checks out. so it's operationally feasible; need the eval results and the synthetic run to be confident.
[08:36] Priya Singh: noted, we'll prioritize cleaning the parser and not handling partial streams in UI.
[08:41] Alex Chen: perfect. recap and next steps: (1) Redwood: share bench sheet, SDK snippets, adaptive batching examples, security doc; (2) Lumina: run synthetic tests, validate schema against their sample dataset, enable KV prefetch; (3) schedule private deployment sizing call week of 11/16 if results look good.
[08:59] Morgan Reyes: agreed. thanks all.
[09:02] Alex Chen: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in the shared doc and I'll send a calendar invite for the sizing call.
[09:08] (meeting ends)
